entries: What is the national flag of India?

India's national flag, the Tiranga, has three horizontal bands: saffron (top), white (middle) and green (bottom), with a navy-blue Ashoka Chakra of 24 spokes in the centre. It was adopted on 22 July 1947 and designed by Pingali Venkayya.
What is the national anthem of India?
India's national anthem is 'Jana Gana Mana', written by Rabindranath Tagore. It takes about 52 seconds to sing and was adopted on 24 January 1950.
What is the national song of India?
India's national song is 'Vande Mataram', written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
What is the national emblem of India?
India's national emblem is the Lion Capital of Ashoka from Sarnath, with the motto 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth alone triumphs).
What is the national bird of India?
The Indian peacock (peafowl) is the national bird of India.
What is the national flower of India?
The lotus is the national flower of India.
What is the national fruit of India?
The mango is the national fruit of India.
What is the national tree of India?
The banyan tree is the national tree of India.
What is the national river of India?
The Ganga (Ganges) is the national river of India.
What is the national aquatic animal of India?
The Gangetic river dolphin is India's national aquatic animal.
What is the national heritage animal of India?
The Indian elephant is India's national heritage animal.
What is the national sport of India?
India has no officially declared national sport, though hockey is often called the national game.
What is the national calendar of India?
India's national calendar is the Saka calendar, adopted in 1957.
What is the national currency of India?
The Indian rupee (₹) is India's currency, issued by the Reserve Bank of India. The ₹ symbol was designed by D. Udaya Kumar in 2010.
India became independent on 15 August 1947, ending British rule.
which year did india get freedom
Republic Day is on 26 January. India's Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950, making India a republic.
Who is the father of the nation of India?
Mahatma Gandhi (Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, 1869–1948) is called the Father of the Nation. He led India's freedom struggle through non-violence (ahimsa) and satyagraha.
Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat. His birthday is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti and the International Day of Non-Violence.
The Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha), led by Gandhi from 12 March to 6 April 1930, was a 390 km walk from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to break the British salt law.
What was the Quit India Movement?
The Quit India Movement was launched by Gandhi on 8 August 1942 with the call 'Do or Die', demanding an end to British rule.
The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–1922), led by Gandhi, asked Indians to boycott British goods, schools and courts. It was called off after the Chauri Chaura incident.
What was the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
On 13 April 1919 in Amritsar, British troops under General Dyer fired on a peaceful crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, killing hundreds.
The revolt of 1857, also called the First War of Indian Independence, began at Meerut on 10 May 1857. Leaders included Mangal Pandey, Rani Lakshmibai, Tantia Tope and Bahadur Shah Zafar.
Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister (1947–1964). His birthday, 14 November, is celebrated as Children's Day.
Who was the first President of India?
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was India's first President (1950–1962).
Who was the first Vice President of India?
Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was India's first Vice President and second President. His birthday, 5 September, is Teachers' Day.
Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?
Indira Gandhi was India's first woman Prime Minister (1966–1977 and 1980–1984).
first woman prime minister of india
Who was the first woman President of India?
Pratibha Patil was India's first woman President (2007–2012).
Who was the first Indian in space?
Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian in space, in 1984 aboard Soyuz T-11. He told Indira Gandhi India looked 'Saare Jahan Se Achha'.
Who was Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam?
Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam (1931–2015), born in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, was a scientist called the 'Missile Man of India' and India's 11th President (2002–2007).
Subhas Chandra Bose ('Netaji') was a freedom fighter who led the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj). He gave the slogan 'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom'.
who gave the slogan give me blood
Bhagat Singh (1907–1931) was a revolutionary freedom fighter, hanged by the British at age 23. He popularised the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'.
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the 'Iron Man of India', was the first Deputy Prime Minister and united over 560 princely states. The Statue of Unity (182 m) honours him.
Who was Dr. B. R. Ambedkar?
Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the chief architect of the Indian Constitution, chairman of its Drafting Committee, and a champion of social justice.
Rabindranath Tagore was a poet who wrote India's national anthem and became the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize (Literature, 1913) for 'Gitanjali'.
Swami Vivekananda was a spiritual leader famous for his 1893 speech in Chicago. His birthday, 12 January, is National Youth Day.
Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi was a queen who fought the British in the revolt of 1857.
Who founded the Indian National Congress?
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume, with W. C. Bonnerjee as its first president.
The Taj Mahal in Agra was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It was built between about 1632 and 1653.
The Red Fort in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan, completed in 1648. The Prime Minister hoists the flag there on Independence Day.
Qutub Minar in Delhi was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak around 1199 and completed by Iltutmish. It is about 73 m tall.
Ashoka the Great was a Mauryan emperor (reigned about 268–232 BCE) who embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga war and spread messages of peace.
Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE, with help from his advisor Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.
Babur founded the Mughal Empire after the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
Akbar (reigned 1556–1605) was the greatest Mughal emperor, known for religious tolerance (Din-i-Ilahi) and his nine court gems (navratnas).
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj (1630–1680) founded the Maratha Empire and was famous for guerrilla warfare and a strong navy.
What is the Indus Valley Civilisation?
The Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilisation flourished about 3300–1300 BCE in present-day Pakistan and north-west India. Its cities, like Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, had planned streets and drains.
When was the Indian Constitution adopted?
The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into effect on 26 January 1950. It is the world's longest written constitution.
when did constitution come into force
What is the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
The Preamble declares India a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic, and promises its citizens Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity.

The six Fundamental Rights in India's Constitution: right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and right to constitutional remedies.
How many Fundamental Duties are there?
There are 11 Fundamental Duties in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
What is the minimum voting age in India?
The voting age in India is 18 years (lowered from 21 by the 61st Amendment in 1989).
The Lok Sabha (House of the People) is the lower house of Parliament. Members are directly elected for 5 years; it can have up to 552 members (543 elected seats now).
how many members in lok sabha
The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is the upper house of Parliament, with up to 250 members. It is a permanent house; one-third of members retire every 2 years.
Who is the head of the Indian state?
The President of India is the constitutional head of state; the Prime Minister leads the government.
What is the Supreme Court of India?
The Supreme Court in New Delhi is India's highest court, headed by the Chief Justice of India. It was established on 28 January 1950.
What is the Reserve Bank of India?
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is India's central bank, set up on 1 April 1935. It issues currency and manages monetary policy. Headquarters: Mumbai.
ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), founded in 1969 by Vikram Sarabhai, is India's space agency, headquartered in Bengaluru.
Chandrayaan-3's lander Vikram landed near the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to land there. 23 August is now National Space Day.
Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) reached Mars orbit on 24 September 2014, making India the first country to reach Mars on its first attempt.
What is the longest river in India?
The Ganga is the longest river in India, about 2,525 km.
What is the highest mountain peak in India?
Kangchenjunga (8,586 m), on the Sikkim–Nepal border, is the highest peak in India.
Which is the longest dam in India?
The Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi in Odisha is the longest dam in India. The Tehri Dam is the highest.
What is the largest desert in India?
The Thar Desert (Great Indian Desert) in Rajasthan is India's largest desert.
Which is the southernmost point of India?
Indira Point in the Nicobar Islands is India's southernmost point. Kanyakumari is the southern tip of the mainland.
What is the standard time of India?
Indian Standard Time (IST) is UTC + 5:30, based on 82.5° E longitude near Mirzapur.
Which state has the longest coastline in India?
Gujarat has the longest coastline of any Indian state.
Which is the largest city in India?
Mumbai is the most populous city in India; Delhi's urban area is also among the world's largest.
What is the Silicon Valley of India?
Bengaluru (Bangalore) is called the Silicon Valley of India.
Which is called the Pink City?
Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is called the Pink City.
Which city is called the City of Joy?
Kolkata is called the City of Joy.
Which state is called God's Own Country?
Kerala is called God's Own Country.
What is the state language of Tamil Nadu?
Tamil is the official language of Tamil Nadu. It was declared India's first classical language in 2004.
What is the state animal of Tamil Nadu?
The Nilgiri tahr is the state animal of Tamil Nadu.
What is the state bird of Tamil Nadu?
The emerald dove is the state bird of Tamil Nadu.
What is the state flower of Tamil Nadu?
The gloriosa lily (senthanthal/kanthal) is the state flower of Tamil Nadu.
What is the state tree of Tamil Nadu?
The palmyra palm (panai maram) is the state tree of Tamil Nadu.
The state was formed on 1 November 1956 as Madras State and renamed Tamil Nadu on 14 January 1969.
when was madras renamed tamil nadu
Thiruvalluvar wrote the Thirukkural, a classic Tamil work of 1,330 couplets (kurals) in 133 chapters on virtue, wealth and love.
Pongal is Tamil Nadu's harvest festival, celebrated in mid-January (Thai month) for four days: Bhogi, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal and Kaanum Pongal.
Jallikattu is a traditional bull-taming sport of Tamil Nadu, held during Pongal. Alanganallur near Madurai is famous for it.
What is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu?
Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu.
K. Kamaraj (1903–1975), Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu (1954–1963), started the free midday meal scheme in schools and is called the 'Kingmaker'.
Subramania Bharati (Mahakavi Bharathiyar, 1882–1921) was a Tamil poet and freedom fighter from Ettayapuram.
Who was V. O. Chidambaram Pillai?
V. O. Chidambaram Pillai ('Kappalottiya Tamizhan') started the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company in 1906 to challenge British shipping.
What are the famous temples of Tamil Nadu?
Famous temples include Meenakshi Amman (Madurai), Brihadeeswarar (Thanjavur, built by Raja Raja Chola I), Ramanathaswamy (Rameswaram), Shore Temple (Mahabalipuram) and Kapaleeshwarar (Chennai).
The Brihadeeswarar (Big) Temple in Thanjavur was built by Raja Raja Chola I and completed in 1010 CE.
Which is the hill station of Tamil Nadu known as the Queen of Hills?
Ooty (Udhagamandalam) in the Nilgiris is called the Queen of Hill Stations. Kodaikanal is called the Princess of Hill Stations.
What is the main river of Tamil Nadu?
The Kaveri (Cauvery) is the main river of Tamil Nadu. Mettur Dam is built on it.
